chunks: Describing your coding experience. The question: What sort of coding experience do you have?
The interviewer is not asking for a list of languages.
They want to know whether you have turned an idea into working code, what kind of code, and whether you can debug it when it fails.
In a hardware role, code is a tool for getting hardware and data work done.
Whatever you mention, they will pick one item and ask how it actually worked, so mention only what you can explain.
A good answer is a small story. It names one project and what it was for.
It says what you did yourself, shows one real technical detail, tells how a bug was found, and ends with a result and a lesson.
A list of language names is like a toolbox with the lid closed. A story shows a tool being used.
A reusable skeleton for any experience answer.
Spend most of your time in the middle: the technical mechanism and the debugging story are what the interviewer remembers and probes.
Firmware: code that runs on a small device such as a microcontroller (a tiny computer on one chip), usually written in C.
Test automation: scripts that run instruments and collect results so measurements can be repeated.
Version control (Git): a system that records changes to code so you can compare and go back.
Debugging method: reproduce the problem, shrink it, form a guess, test the guess, and fix it. Scripting: short programs, often in Python, that automate tasks.
Here is a skeleton with [placeholders] to fill with true details, never invented ones.
"My biggest project was [what it did] , in [language] , and I was responsible for [your part] . The interesting part was [one technical mechanism] .
When it failed, I found the cause by [your method] . The result was [a measurable outcome] , and I learned [a lesson] .
I am strongest in [language] and I am building depth in [another] by [a concrete step] ." That is the whole idea.
"My coding is mostly applied to hardware work. The biggest example is [project] , where I wrote [language] to [goal] .
The interesting technical part was [one specific mechanism] , and I debugged it by [method] . It ended up [measured result] .
Beyond that I've used C for embedded work, Python for scripting and plotting, and Git for version control. I'm strongest in [language] and actively building depth in [other] ."
